definition: A set is a collection of distinct elements, with no positions and no duplicates. The operations that matter are adding, removing, and testing membership. A hash table or a balanced tree is the usual implementation.
details: Putting an element in twice leaves one copy. Order of iteration is not part of the idea, though a particular implementation may define one.

complexity.time: Membership is O(1) average with hashing, or O(log n) in a balanced tree.
complexity.space: O(n) space for the elements themselves.

examples: The set of user ids already processed
The letters that appear in a word, each once
